title: Prediction Registry v1

canonical_node.axiom: Predictions must be recorded before later interpretation, under a shared comparison regime, with failure made visible.
definitions: Prediction: a claim about model behavior under explicit conditions, recorded before tuning.
Test rule: the explicit comparison procedure used to evaluate a prediction.
Pass: the model behaved as claimed under the tested regime.
Failure: the wording, derivation, or equation form must be revised, downgraded, or rejected.
Wrong control: a deliberately incorrect variant that should fail under the same bench.
derivation: The registry sits between claiming the framework is proven and pretending formal work means nothing.
The right claim is that current equations generate testable behavior under a shared comparison regime, and those behaviors can be frozen before later interpretation.

The registry records predictions, states test rules before results, makes failure visible, separates formal structure from theological interpretation, and provides a neighboring verification layer to Lean 4.

The variation audit showed that bare variation with respect to x(t) does not insert entropy directly into the equation of motion; entropy enters only when coupled to the varied coordinate, when chi is the varied field, or when extra dissipative structure is introduced.
This negative result is surfaced as a serious verification layer should.
canonical_node.action: Maintain a registry of preregistered predictions with explicit test rules, record results before interpretation, and ensure wrong controls fail under the same bench.
boundary: This registry does not prove Theophysics true.
It does not claim that the framework is already proven.
It does not treat any single tool (Lean 4, Python, website) as sufficient by itself.
It does not claim full Noether results beyond algebraic invariants.
test: For each prediction, verify that the test rule is stated before the result is known.
Check that failures are visible and lead to revision, downgrade, or rejection.
Verify that wrong controls fail under the same bench as the canonical model.
Check that the variation audit's negative result is preserved and not hidden.

dg1_dependencies: Lean 4 formal proof layer (as neighboring verification)
dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a preregistration and wrong-control rejection layer that freezes predictions before later interpretation, complementing Lean 4 and Python.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the distinction between formal structure and theological interpretation, and keeps negative results visible.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: Without this registry, predictions could be tuned after results, wrong controls might pass unnoticed, and the verification stack would lose its preregistration layer.

overstatement_risks: Interpreting registry passes as proof of Theophysics truth.
Treating algebraic invariants as full Noether results.
Assuming the registry alone is sufficient for verification.
kill_conditions: If predictions are recorded after results are known.
If wrong controls pass under the same bench.
risk.lean_target: Formalize the test rule and pass/fail criteria as a specification for the registry.

plain_summary: This document establishes a prediction registry that preregisters testable claims, states test rules before results, and makes failures visible. It records several passing predictions and a negative variation audit result, positioning itself as a verification layer alongside Lean 4 and Python, without claiming proof of Theophysics.
